subject: SLA remediation & credit calculation request - NovaPulse outage
messages:
From: Alex Novak <alex.novak@novapulse.io>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samantha Rai <samantha.rai@novapulse.io>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 09:18:00 +0000
Subject: Request for SLA credit after 2026-01-11 outage

Hi Marcus / Marissa,

Thanks again for the quick incident updates overnight. We experienced a significant service disruption on our inference endpoints on 2026-01-11 that materially impacted traffic for our production users. Per our contract (SLA Section 4.2), we'd like to request confirmation of credit eligibility and a calculation for the affected billing period.

Summary from our side:
- Window we observed: 2026-01-11 03:20 UTC -> 2026-01-11 03:54 UTC (approx. 34 minutes)
- Error pattern: 503s + increased latency; traffic failed to be served by fallback region for ~18 minutes
- Traffic affected: all calls to api.redwood.ai/v1/generate (region: us-west)

Please confirm:
1) Whether NovaPulse meets the criteria for a service credit under the SLA.
2) The formula and inputs you will use to calculate the credit (we'd like an auditable CSV).
3) Estimated timeline for issuance and whether it will apply to our next invoice or as a credit note.

Attaching our local logs and a short sample trace (not included here). Appreciate a point estimate so we can close our internal ticketing.

Best,
Alex Novak
Head of Platform Reliability
NovaPulse

---
Attachment stubs: sample_trace_20260111.txt (text), logs_excerpt_01.json (text)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Novak <alex.novak@novapulse.io>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 12:04:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Request for SLA credit after 2026-01-11 outage

Thanks Alex — and sorry for the disruption. Looping in Monica (AM) and Tessa (Billing/Finance ops) to validate eligibility and drive the credit.

Internal notes / asks:
- Monica: can you confirm NovaPulse's committed monthly charge and whether this incident falls under their Dedicated contract SLO? My read: incident appears to meet a downtime threshold in SLA clause 4.2 (>=30 consecutive minutes of unavailable).
- Tessa: please start the preliminary credit calc using the SLA formula (see below) and prepare an audit CSV we can send to the customer. Include timestamps and the calculation steps.

SLA calc approach (proposed):
1) Confirm exact outage window from metrics/ingestion (we should reconcile our server-side observed window with NovaPulse's).
2) Downtime fraction = total unavailable minutes in billing period / total minutes in billing period.
3) Credit = min(downtime fraction * monthly committed fee, cap per SLA) — also apply the discrete credit band if SLA uses step bands (e.g., 10% for 30-120min).

I've created a JIRA for the postmortem and linked metrics: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-5123
I'll follow up once Monica and Tessa confirm numbers.

Thanks,
Marcus
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Novak <alex.novak@novapulse.io>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 15:22:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Request for SLA credit after 2026-01-11 outage

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear summary. We reviewed the incident and the billing record for NovaPulse. Below is our preliminary determination and calculation; attaching the detailed CSV file.

Incident determination:
- Official server-side outage window (reconciled): 2026-01-11 03:18:00 UTC -> 2026-01-11 03:54:00 UTC (36 minutes total)
- This meets the SLA clause for unavailability >= 30 consecutive minutes.

Calculation summary (attached: sla-credit-calculation.csv):
- Billing period (Jan 2026): 31 days = 44640 minutes
- Downtime minutes counted: 36
- Downtime fraction = 36 / 44640 = 0.000806 (0.0806%)
- Monthly committed fee (contract DL-78923): USD 12,000 (monthly Dedicated commitment)
- Raw prorated credit = 0.000806 * 12,000 = USD 9.67
- SLA discrete banding: per Section 4.2, any outage >=30 minutes triggers a standard 10% service credit of the monthly committed fee (whichever is greater between prorated and banded credit).
- Final credit to issue = 10% * 12,000 = USD 1,200

Notes:
- We are applying the banded credit (10%) because it exceeds the raw prorated amount. This follows prior precedent for Dedicated customers.
- Attached CSV includes: start/end timestamps, metric source, calculation steps, and a digital sign-off line for audit.

Next steps / timeline:
- Internal approval: Tessa to raise the credit memo with Finance (expected 3 business days).
- Customer-facing: we'll issue a credit note (CN-2026-0112) to NovaPulse which will be applied to the Feb invoice unless you prefer an immediate refund.
- Postmortem PDF (incident_postmortem_NovaPulse.pdf) will be shared once the engineering write-up is finished (ETA 2026-01-15).

Wanted to be transparent on the math — happy to walk through the CSV if you'd like.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Account Manager, Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: sla-credit-calculation.csv (CSV, includes line-by-line calc and meter reconciliations)

From: Alex Novak <alex.novak@novapulse.io>

1) Please send the formal credit note (CN-2026-0112) and confirm it will appear on the Feb 2026 invoice.
2) Can you share the final incident postmortem PDF when available (we'll use it for our internal RCA distribution)?

If those are straightforward, please proceed and mark this ticket resolved from our side.

Best regards,
Alex Novak

NovaPulse
